Let's analyze Devin's work, step-by-step, to see if he made any mistakes.

### Step 1

In Step 1, Devin wrote $\dfrac{d}{dx}(-3x-11)$ as the difference of two separate derivatives $\dfrac{d}{dx}(-3x)-\dfrac{d}{dx}(11)$, using the **difference rule.**

This step is perfectly fine.

### Step 2

In Step 2, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(-3x)$ was kept as it is, and $\dfrac{d}{dx}(11)$ was rewritten as $0$, using the **constant rule.**

Indeed, according to the constant rule, the derivative of a constant number is equal to zero.

This step is perfectly fine.

### Step 3

In Step 3, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(-3x)$ was rewritten as $-3\dfrac{d}{dx}(x)$ using the **constant multiple rule.**

This step is perfectly fine.

### Steps 4 & 5

In Steps 4 & 5, Devin evaluated $-3\dfrac{d}{dx}(x)$ as $-3$, which was correct of him.

### Summary

Devin did not make a mistake.

question.content:
Devin tried to find the derivative of $-3x-11$ using basic differentiation rules. Here is his work:

$\begin{align}
&&&\phantom{=}\dfrac{d}{dx}(-3x-11)
\\\\
\text{Step 1}
&&&=\dfrac{d}{dx}(-3x)-\dfrac{d}{dx}(11)
\\\\
\text{Step 2}
&&&=\dfrac{d}{dx}(-3x)-0
\\\\
\text{Step 3}
&&&=-3\dfrac{d}{dx}(x)
\\\\
\text{Step 4}
&&&=-3\cdot 1
\\\\
\text{Step 5}
&&&=-3
\end{align}$

**At which step did Devin make a mistake, if at all?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.content: Devin did not make a mistake
